source: PLAN §0 OR19 + §4.3 "App errors reach the agent, always"
note: Coalescing cases: one state (= one chat) from emptyState(); for each entry in `events` (ordered by `at`, ms after now0) call coalesce(state, ev, now0 + at) — or flush(state, now0 + at) when the entry is `{at, flush:true}`, or setRunning(state, instance, rev) (no delivery) when it is `{at, setRunning:{instance, rev}}` — and compare with the same-index `expect`: delivered (deliver !== null), reason (the returned reason), summary (deliver.summary), records (deliver.records.length), instance (deliver.instance), count / newCount (when delivered: the last delivered record; otherwise the open record for ev.fingerprint), pending ({instance → state.pending[instance].length, missing = 0}), overflow ({instance → state.overflow[instance], missing = 0}). Other cases: fn ∈ fingerprint(input) | fromFrontendReport(input, now, opts) → {ok, ev} | {ok, reason} | formatForAgent(delivery, opts) with `contains` substrings and `maxLength`.

cases.name: three same-fingerprint build errors in 2 min → one delivery (count 1), the rest fold (record count 3)
a fourth at +11 min (past the 10-min fold window) → a new delivery carrying count 4
the fold window counts from the last DELIVERY, not the last event: 0, 9, 18 min → two deliveries
eight distinct fingerprints in 5 min → six deliveries, two capped, a flush while still capped is a no-op (pending kept), one "+2 more" when the hour reopens
a capped fingerprint seen again folds into its pending record; the summary carries the count
a new event arriving as the hour reopens rides along in the "+N more" delivery (merged), never waits
rev 3 after rev 4 → dropped (stale-rev): a fleet ship restarting every host is not news
a newer rev resets the fold and the cap: the same file:line failing at rev 5 lands at once
setRunning is the registration fact: a rev that built clean is silence, and a late error from the older rev is stale-rev

rev contract: a host restart re-registers its persisted rev (no reset, the fold holds); a host that lost its counter re-registers lower and is still heard (registration is authoritative, never a silent channel)
the cap is per instance: a second app keeps its own six, and its event leaves the first app's pending untouched
the chat cap (12/h across apps): two apps × 7 fill it; a third app's first error is chat-capped; every pending drains one flush at a time when the hour reopens
bounded pending: a storm of 36 distinct fingerprints → 6 delivered, 20 pending + 10 overflow, one "+30 more" with 20 records when the hour reopens
invalid events are refused with a schema reason and change nothing
